keyFindings: Cushioning: The Gara Carbon 2 is generally soft and well-cushioned in the heel/midfoot with a comfortable, somewhat plush feel, but it is less aggressive than premium super-soles and can feel clunky at very early contact due to the geometry.

Responsiveness: It is described as soft and bouncy with moderate energy return, better for tempo to marathon-style efforts than all-out 5k–10k speed; reviewers say the ride is less propulsive and not highly responsive.

Stability: Overall stability is a weakness for this model, with noted foot translation during turns and an explicit “not stable” verdict, though the toe box/midfoot overlays and lacing can improve lockdown for some runners.
Durability: Outsole durability is below average for a super shoe, with average traction but a lateral heel piece tearing off around 40 miles and quick midsole wear after the opening in the outsole.

Cushioning: The shoe is notably soft and plush—described as soft foam with a very cushioned heel collar and comfortable long-run comfort, but multiple testers call it softer than an ideal racer and better suited for distance/training mileage.
Responsiveness: It has a bouncy, light, and comfortable ride with good bounce, yet several reviewers say it is not as snappy or “pop”y as other modern carbon-plated race shoes.

Stability: Fit and lockdown are strong (heel-to-midfoot secure), but testers report fewer support cues for overpronation, a lower-riding heel collar that can affect longer-run stability, and generally rate it as a neutral-stability platform.

Durability: The review repeatedly highlights a grippy Duratech 5000 outsole and premium materials, but does not provide direct evidence of outsole wear or long-term material longevity from usage testing.

Cushioning: The shoe uses a 40 mm heel / 35 mm forefoot stack (5 mm drop) and is described as “squishy without falling into soft territory,” giving a soft, controlled heel-to-forefoot ride that stays comfortable over distance.
Responsiveness: The Anima PBX midsole is repeatedly called “bouncy” with “noticeable energy return,” and the ride is praised as pleasant for faster paces, indicating good snappiness and rebound.

Stability: Fit is reported as strong with a premium Matryx upper that “wraps the foot,” but the review does not directly assess torsional rigidity, heel-counter firmness, or lateral support, so those aspects are not clearly evaluated.

Durability: The outsole was intentionally detailed for longevity and the Matryx upper is noted for durability, which points to positive outsole wear and material longevity expectations, though no long-term wear mileage evidence is provided.

specsDecision: No automatic score/spec change proposed. Conflicts were recorded for reviewer decision.
